subject: After-action: Acme Health lead attribution and rebate request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@eventreg.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Post-event packet and attendee/pipeline dump — Acme Health booth

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for sponsoring the Redwood booth at CloudConnect last week. Per our wrap checklist I’m attaching the attendee export we pulled from the scanner and a first-pass pipeline export for leads marked as ACME in HubSpot. Quick summary up front:

- Total scanned badge swipes associated with Acme reps: 128
- Leads created in HubSpot tagged to ACME campaign: 42
- Opportunities closed this quarter that trace to event leads: 3 (combined ACV: $152,000)

We’re seeing a mismatch between the scanned attendees and the leads that made it into your CRM; Tom, any chance the event reg exports included opt-out flags we should be aware of?

Attachments: event_attendee_list_acme.csv (scanner export), pipeline_export_q3_acme.xlsx (HubSpot extract), signed-sponsorship-sow-acme.pdf

Next steps proposed:
1) Sarah: confirm which attendee rows should be considered marketing-qualified for your rebate calculation (we used opt-in + job title filters).
2) Ben/Rachel: reconcile HubSpot lead source mapping for the 128 scanned badges vs. the 42 leads.
3) If needed, propose a split for crediting partially qualified leads (recommendation below).

Recommended split for disputed leads (suggested policy): 50/50 credit split for leads that scanned at the booth but were routed to a partner contact and thus not tagged to ACME campaign in HubSpot. This protects both sides while we finalize canonical ownership.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the sheets — I’m free Thu 16th 10–11am PT.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Field Marketing Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0126

From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@eventreg.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 12:38:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-event packet and attendee/pipeline dump — Acme Health booth

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for sending these over. We appreciate the quick turnaround. A few points up front:

1) Our rebate calculation is tied to Marketing Qualified Leads as defined in our SOW (page 2). That requires verified contact info + healthcare buyer title. From a quick scan, 22 of the 128 scanned rows are internal Acme staff or contractors and should not count.
2) We only see 15 of the 42 HubSpot leads matching the badge IDs in your attendee export — the remaining 27 appear to have been attributed to partner follow-ups (we’ve asked our SDR team to pull notes).
3) Because the SOW ties rebate thresholds to qualified leads only, we can’t accept a blanket 50/50 split for leads that were routed elsewhere. We propose a verification step: our SDR manager will confirm which of the disputed 27 meet the MQL definition within 7 business days; if fewer than 10 qualify, Acme requests a partial credit of 25% of the promised rebate.

I’ve attached a short spreadsheet (we’ll send privately) with our initial tagging — Tom, can you confirm whether the event reg output includes internal staff flags and whether the badge IDs map consistently across systems?

Best,
Sarah Jensen
Director, Partnerships — Acme Health
sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-event packet and attendee/pipeline dump — Acme Health booth

Hi Sarah —

Totally understand and thanks for the specifics. We want to be consistent with the SOW and avoid surprises. Action items from our side:

- Ben and Rachel will run the HubSpot lead history to pull notes + assigned owner for the 27 disputed leads and tag any that match Acme contact info.
- I’ll ask events operations to re-run the scanner export to flag badge types (exhibitor, staff, attendee) and send a cleaned file. Tom — if you confirm whether internal staff flags exist in the reg export that will speed things up.

If the verification shows >=10 of the disputed 27 meet the MQL definition, Redwood will honor the original rebate schedule. If <10 qualify, we’re open to the 25% partial credit approach you suggested. Can we aim to close this by EOD Friday (18 Sep)?

I’m standing by for Tom/Ben/Rachel.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:11:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-event packet and attendee/pipeline dump — Acme Health booth

Sarah —

Quick update from the HubSpot side: I pulled the hub export and matched badge IDs where present. Findings:
- 15 leads are direct matches to scanner badge IDs and were tagged to ACME campaign (these are the 3 closed opps + 12 open).
- 8 leads have scanner badge IDs but were routed to partner-segment owners; notes indicate partner follow-up after booth intro.
- 4 leads have incomplete emails or generic addresses (e.g., contact@company.com) and failed our MQL criteria.

I don’t see any indication in the HubSpot notes that Redwood intentionally untagged Acme leads — this looks like partner routing behavior in the field. Given that, I support the verification step Marissa proposed. If our SDR checks confirm even 6–9 of the disputed group meet MQL, I’d recommend Redwood offer a 40% credit (compromise) instead of 50/50 or 25% — it splits risk but recognizes that Acme did engage at the booth.

If helpful, we can set up a 20-minute call Fri 18 Sep 10am PT to show the matching logic.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 17:24:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-event packet and attendee/pipeline dump — Acme Health booth

Hi all —

Thanks for the rapid responses. I’m stepping in to finalize this so we can close the quarter cleanly. Decision (per SOW guidance and the verification window already agreed):

1) Redwood will accept Acme’s verification period of 7 business days for the disputed 27 leads. Rachel, please coordinate with Acme SDRs and provide a confirmed list by Tue 22 Sep EOB.
2) If >=10 additional leads qualify as MQLs, Redwood honors the full rebate schedule.
3) If 6–9 qualify, Redwood will issue a 40% credit toward the rebate (Ben’s compromise).
4) If <=5 qualify, Redwood will issue a 25% partial credit.

We’ll also commit to adding an explicit badge-type flag to the post-event packet going forward so sponsor calculations have a single canonical field to reference. Marissa — please own that process improvement.

Sarah/Tom — thanks for working with us on the verification. Laura Bennett
VP, Field Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
